summary: Brent nearing $120 on repeated Houthi strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure is no longer just an energy story — it's now visibly hitting Indian trade flows (Morbi ceramic exports down 40%, ABDL margins squeezed), while two confirmed Cabinet/regulator decisions (the ₹10,000cr Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme and IRDAI's draft insurance-distribution caps) and a hardening EMS memory-cost shock (Lava's Nov-15 price hike) give the system new, dated, quantified beneficiary and headwind calls.

themes.thesis: Repeated Houthi strikes on Saudi refineries keep crude near $120 and India's import basket above it, lifting upstream realisations while the same war is now directly cutting Gulf-bound export volumes and raising input/freight costs for companies far outside the energy sector.
